groups.name: hyphen
groups.description: A tight hyphen between two Latin or Cyrillic words, when the shorter has at most 3 letters, gets a word joiner after it, so a line never breaks after it (UAX #14 already forbids a break before it). Longer pairs, other scripts and identifiers are left alone (see hyphen-guards and guards.json)

groups.name: hyphen-guards
groups.description: The hyphen rule needs a Latin or Cyrillic letter on both sides and declines in an unspaced run that looks like an identifier: one containing /, @, _ or a period followed by a letter or digit. It reads the whole run, not the neighbors of one hyphen, so every hyphen in a run gets the same decision. Everything else is a missed edit by design

groups.name: em-dash-rules
groups.description: placeEmdash alone, en. A dash changes its glyph only; the one whitespace edit is a regular space before it becoming U+00A0. A tight double hyphen needs a classified token on both sides (a word, number, currency sign, bracket or a classified quote) and is left alone between two numbers. A spaced one needs a word, number, closing bracket, sentence punctuation or closing quote on the left and something that is not sentence punctuation on the right; a single hyphen needs a word on the left and a word, number or currency sign on the right, or ! ? , on the left and a word on the right. A dash at line start needs horizontal whitespace and a word after it. A typed em dash gets the no-break space only. Anything with a missing or unclassified neighbor is a missed edit
